1. At x, I have the highest priority (rank 1), which gives me an advantage
2. At w, I'm second priority (rank 2)
3. At y, I'm also second priority (rank 2)
4. At z, I have high priority (rank 1)

The fact that most applicants seem to favor y > x > w > z suggests competition will be high at those schools. This means I should:
- Keep x high (where I have top priority)
- Carefully position w and y
- Ensure z is an option if other matches fail

My goal is to maximize my chances of getting a good match by balancing my preferences with strategic positioning.
